text.system: You score free-text answers from an FSU undergraduate's research-lab matching survey. From the text alone, rate the student's interest on four axes: computational (modeling, simulation, analyzing neural data, AI), cognitive (behavior, decision-making, memory, perception in people), organism (hands-on work with animals or tissue), clinical (disorders and their treatment). Use 1-5 (1 none, 3 moderate, 5 central to what they wrote) or null when the text gives no evidence either way. Never infer from absence: a text about human memory says nothing about animals, so organism is null, not 1. Add 1-5 short topic tags (e.g. 'working memory', 'sleep', 'BCI') and quote the phrase that most drove your scores.

questions.notes: Structured answers feed the statistical classifier directly. free_text answers are scored by Haiku into the same feature space at match time. Nothing from the transcript field is stored; it is parsed client-side into course codes and titles only.

classifier_targets.axis_computational: 1-5: interest in how neurons/circuits compute, modeling, data analysis
classifier_targets.axis_cognitive: 1-5: interest in behavior, decision-making, memory, perception in people
classifier_targets.axis_organism: 1-5: interest in / comfort with animal models and wet-lab work
classifier_targets.axis_clinical: 1-5: interest in disorders, treatment, clinical relevance
classifier_targets.career_goal: one of [phd, md, md_phd, industry_ml, industry_other, undecided]
classifier_targets.project_length: one of [dis_one_semester, dis_multi_semester, honors_thesis, urop, volunteer_first]

labs.name: Nee Lab
labs.dept: Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Cognitive control and working memory in humans, building models of directed prefrontal interactions from fMRI and testing them with TMS.
labs.how_to_apply: Email CV, unofficial transcript, and letter of intent to neesubjects@psy.fsu.edu; remote DIS available; Psych/Neuro/CS/Stats majors preferred.
labs.entry_point: Nee (2021) eLife, integrative frontal-parietal dynamics supporting cognitive control.

labs.name: Martin Lab
labs.dept: Psychology
labs.focus: Cognitive neuroscience of human memory.
labs.how_to_apply: Email CV, 300-500 word research/career interest statement, and unofficial transcript to cmartin@psy.fsu.edu.

labs.name: Learning Brain Lab
labs.dept: Psychology
labs.focus: Developmental cognitive neuroscience of attention, learning, and mental health in children and teens using fMRI.
labs.how_to_apply: Fill out the undergraduate application form linked on the DIS listing.
labs.expectations: At least 9 hours/week (3 credits), weekly lab meetings, participant recruitment and data collection.

labs.name: BRAINS Lab
labs.dept: Psychology (Clinical)
labs.focus: Biobehavioral research on addiction and internalizing syndromes.
labs.how_to_apply: Email graduate student Zoe Howell at howell@psy.fsu.edu; lab accepts students with no prior experience.
labs.expectations: Running participants, making conference posters, weekly lab meetings, recruitment.

labs.name: Bertram Lab
labs.dept: Mathematics (Biomathematics) / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Mathematical neuroscience and physiology: neural coding in taste and smell, bursting neurons, hormone secretion, network science.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab has historically taken students from Math, Biology, and Neuroscience, so email asking if accepting DIS students.
labs.entry_point: NSF-funded project with Vincis applying network-science tools to taste-coding neural data.

labs.name: Karamched Lab
labs.dept: Mathematics (Biomathematics) / Molecular Biophysics / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Biomathematics, stochastic processes, complex systems, and cellular neuroscience.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; runs the Biomathematics journal club, which is a natural first contact.
labs.entry_point: Collaborates with Bertram and Storace on the neural basis of smell.

labs.name: Asllani Lab
labs.dept: Mathematics (Biomathematics affiliate)
labs.focus: Complex systems and network science.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process.

labs.name: Vincis Lab
labs.dept: Biological Science / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Neural basis of taste and ingestive behavior in rodents.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab has had undergrad lab techs, so email asking about DIS.
labs.entry_point: Joint NSF project with Bertram on patterns of neural activity coding taste.

labs.name: Storace Lab
labs.dept: Biological Science / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Neural basis of the sense of smell.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process.
labs.entry_point: Collaborates with Bertram and Karamched on olfaction.

labs.name: Wilber Lab
labs.dept: Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Brain dynamics of spatial orientation and rodent models of Alzheimer's disease (focus line needs confirmation from lab page).
labs.how_to_apply: Appears in the Psychology DIS directory; confirm listed process.

labs.name: D. Fadool Lab
labs.dept: Biological Science / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Olfactory neuroscience (focus line needs confirmation from lab page).
labs.how_to_apply: Lab site has a Positions page; check it first.

labs.name: Varela Lab
labs.dept: Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Thalamic circuit mechanisms of learning and memory across sleep and wake: sleep spindles, closed-loop control of sleep oscillations, and deviance detection that updates cortical predictive models.
labs.how_to_apply: Lab page invites interested students to contact Dr. Varela (c.varela@fsu.edu) with a CV and brief research interests; backgrounds in CS, physics, and engineering explicitly welcomed.
labs.expectations: Funded by NIMH, Whitehall Foundation, and Alzheimer's Association; Apr 2026 ad sought postbacc/PhD/postdoc researchers.
labs.entry_point: Varela et al. 2024, Frontiers in Neuroscience: thalamic deviance detection as a predictive-processing mechanism (DOI 10.3389/fnins.2024.1359180).

labs.name: Kira Lab
labs.dept: Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: How cortical circuits support generalization and flexible decision-making in mice navigating virtual-reality tasks.
labs.how_to_apply: Has a UROP mentor listing (Aug 2025: not currently looking, 2 RA slots, email skira@fsu.edu); UROP students presented at the 2026 Undergraduate Research Symposium, so check UROP first.
labs.expectations: Recommended: basic neuroscience, basic MATLAB/Python, strong analytical skills; RAs present findings at lab meetings.
labs.entry_point: Kira et al. 2023, Nature Communications: mixed-selectivity population code for flexible navigation decisions (DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-37804-2).

labs.name: Moberly Lab
labs.dept: Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: How learning and neuromodulation (acetylcholine) reconfigure cortical circuit dynamics during sensory-guided and fear learning in mice.
labs.how_to_apply: New lab (recruiting a grad student for Fall 2027); no posted undergrad process; email ahm26b@fsu.edu.
labs.entry_point: Moberly, Cardin & Higley 2025, bioRxiv: learning-dependent cholinergic plasticity reconfigures cortical circuit dynamics (DOI 10.1101/2025.11.10.687664).

labs.name: Takagi Lab
labs.dept: Biological Science / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: How olfactory circuits and sensory-guided behavior evolve across Drosophila species, including how diet shifts affect brain function.
labs.how_to_apply: Lab opened Spring 2026 and is accepting grad students; no posted undergrad process yet; check takagilab.org.
labs.entry_point: Takagi et al. 2025, Cell Reports: olfactory projection neuron rewiring in an ecological specialist (DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2025.115615).

labs.name: Needham Lab
labs.dept: Mathematics
labs.focus: Geometry and topology for data science: optimal transport, Gromov-Wasserstein distances, and topological data analysis applied to networks, biology, and interpretable ML.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; department page lists office hours MTWR 11-12 in LOV 309, a natural first contact.
labs.entry_point: NSF-funded project with Martin Bauer on generalized optimal transport models for images, shapes, and networks (2025).

labs.name: Schmidt Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology (Clinical) - Anxiety and Behavioral Health Clinic
labs.focus: Etiology, prevention, and treatment of anxiety disorders and associated psychopathology (social anxiety, panic, GAD, OCD, PTSD).
labs.how_to_apply: Email Timothy McDermott, PhD (tmcdermott@psy.fsu.edu) and state if you are interested in the neurophysiological (EEG) track.
labs.bridge: The DIS listing offers a separate 'neurophysiology' track with EEG research, giving pre-clinical students exposure to neural data inside an anxiety-treatment lab.
labs.expectations: Minimum 3.5 GPA; at least a two-semester commitment; weekly hours not stated.
labs.entry_point: Neurophysiology (EEG) DIS track within the anxiety-disorder studies described on the DIS page.

labs.name: Children's Learning Clinic
labs.dept: Department of Psychology (Clinical) - Children's Learning Clinic (co-mentor Leah Singh, Director)
labs.focus: ADHD and the neurocognitive factors (e.g., executive function) underlying it, including development of neurocognitive training protocols for children.
labs.how_to_apply: Email a CV/resume, unofficial degree audit, and brief letter of interest to clc@psy.fsu.edu about 4 weeks before the end of the semester prior to starting; openings depend on graduating RAs.
labs.bridge: Executive-function and working-memory task data in a clinical child population is the kind of behavioral dataset that cognitive models are fit to; the site mentions no neural recording, so treat this as behavior-first (needs confirmation).
labs.expectations: GPA 3.5 or higher; minimum one-year (3 semesters) commitment at 10 hours per week; weekly lab meeting; sophomore/junior standing or UROP acceptance.
labs.entry_point: Serving as an 'Executive Function Coach' for children with ADHD and assisting lab data work, per the students page.

labs.name: Kaschak Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology (Cognition and Cognitive Neuroscience) - Learning, Memory, and Language Lab
labs.focus: How people get meaning from language, how language patterns shift with others' behavior, and how memory and other cognitive capacities shape language use.
labs.how_to_apply: Email Dr. Kaschak at kaschak@psy.fsu.edu with 'DIS' as the subject line; face-to-face and remote DIS options are offered.
labs.bridge: A behavioral language-and-memory lab that suits students heading toward computational psycholinguistics or language-model-based cognitive science; no neural methods are stated on the page.
labs.expectations: GPA above 3.0 and a two-semester commitment; hours not stated.
labs.entry_point: Helping develop and run language comprehension/production experiments and attending lab meetings.

labs.name: BARC Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology (Cognition and Cognitive Neuroscience / Developmental / Neuroscience); core faculty, Florida Center for Reading Research
labs.focus: The Brain Analysis of Reading and Cognition (B.A.R.C.) Lab studies how brain function, attention, and reading interrelate, including dyslexia and ADHD, using neuroimaging and neuromodulation.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; faculty page lists cna25@fsu.edu and notes graduate recruiting for Fall 2027.
labs.bridge: Multimodal fMRI/TMS reading data in children and adults is a direct on-ramp to network-level analysis of reading circuits; no undergraduate route is posted, so students would need to inquire (needs confirmation).

labs.name: HEAR Lab
labs.dept: School of Communication Science and Disorders - Hearing and Aging Research (HEAR) Laboratory
labs.focus: Uses cognitive neuroscience tools to study the brain mechanisms of speech understanding and how they change with aging, hearing loss, or listening to nonnative speakers.
labs.how_to_apply: The Get Involved page says the lab is 'always on the lookout for undergraduate and graduate students' and links a short Microsoft Forms application; contact hearlab@cci.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: One of the few human-subjects labs at FSU that explicitly pairs EEG with machine learning; the team page lists six current undergraduate RAs, making it a realistic entry for CSD or psychology students (ML depth needs confirmation).
labs.entry_point: Speech-in-noise EEG/psychophysics studies of aging and hearing loss described on the lab home page.

labs.name: NoLaB
labs.dept: School of Communication Science & Disorders - Neurobiology of Language and Behavior (NoLaB) Lab
labs.focus: Structural brain imaging of lesion and atrophy patterns linked to language behavior in stroke and progressive aphasias, including MRI- and AI-based metrics of natural language production.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; directory lists sl24y@fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Brain-behavior mapping in aphasia with automatically extracted language features is a computational-adjacent clinical neuroscience path for CSD students; no undergraduate route is posted (needs confirmation).
labs.entry_point: Lukic et al. 2024, Cortex: discriminating PPA variants with automatically extracted morphosyntactic measures from connected speech.

labs.name: MSD Lab
labs.dept: School of Communication Science and Disorders - Motor Speech Disorders Lab (MSDLab)
labs.focus: How listeners understand and adapt to dysarthric speech (from stroke, TBI, Parkinson disease, ALS), with the goal of improving communication by training listeners.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab site lists kaitlin.lansford@cci.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: A perceptual-learning lab on disordered speech that serves CSD/pre-SLP students directly; the lab site says the team includes undergraduate researchers, but no join process is posted.
labs.entry_point: Current project on treating dysarthric speech via perceptual listening training (lab home page).

labs.name: Hammock Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Neurobiological mechanisms of social and affective behavior in developing and mature mammals, within an evolutionary framework.
labs.how_to_apply: Complete the interest survey linked on the DIS page (https://fsu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9Yz4QvfUSvsUtz7).
labs.bridge: A wet-lab behavioral neuroscience entry point for students who want organism-level grounding (social behavior circuits) before moving to quantitative behavior analysis.

labs.name: Rinaman Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: Development, anatomy, and function of brain-gut circuits that control stress responsiveness and motivated behavior.
labs.how_to_apply: DIS page says hands-on laboratory research is available with 'a few course prerequisites'; inquire with Dr. Rinaman (no email or form posted).
labs.bridge: Hands-on circuit anatomy in a rodent stress/feeding model gives organism-level intuition for students who later want to model interoceptive or neuroendocrine circuits.
labs.expectations: Some course prerequisites required (not specified on the page).

labs.name: Wang Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology / Program in Neuroscience (Wang Lab; DIS mentor is Research Faculty Yan Liu)
labs.focus: Neuroendocrine basis of social attachment and stress buffering in the monogamous prairie vole, including interactions between social reward and drug reward.
labs.how_to_apply: Email Dr. Yan Liu at yliu2@fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Classic behavioral neuroendocrinology with a strong undergraduate role in behavior scoring and histology; good for students who want wet-lab grounding before quantitative behavior analysis (Zuoxin Wang no longer appears on the faculty roster; Yan Liu is the listed mentor).
labs.expectations: Wants students who are dedicated, hard-working, and reliable; hours not stated.
labs.entry_point: Setting up and scoring vole social-behavior experiments and processing brain tissue for histology.

labs.name: Dewan Lab
labs.dept: Department of Psychology / Program in Neuroscience
labs.focus: How sensory (olfactory) perception is mapped and encoded in the mouse brain using genetic, optogenetic, optical imaging, and behavioral techniques.
labs.how_to_apply: Complete the Dewan Lab Undergraduate RA Interest Form (https://fsu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cYibwJTAhLDPF6m); questions to lab manager pauley@psy.fsu.edu or dewan@psy.fsu.edu; Federal Work Study job ID 57697 noted for a Fall 2024 opening.
labs.bridge: Sensory coding with imaging and behavioral data in mice is the organism-side counterpart to encoding models; undergraduates start with colony care and data handling, so expect a long on-ramp.
labs.expectations: Minimum two-year commitment, DIS credit enrollment, weekend availability for colony work; students should be 'smart, reliable, hard-working'.
labs.entry_point: Mouse colony care and data entry/cleaning as a first role, per the DIS page.

labs.name: Meyer-Baese Lab
labs.dept: Department of Scientific Computing
labs.focus: Medical imaging (pattern recognition for breast MRI, computer-aided diagnosis, fMRI data analysis), computational biology (gene regulatory network dynamics), and computational neuroscience (brain-based classification techniques, nonlinear stability of cortical systems, graph theory on cortical networks).
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; department page lists only a personal homepage (people.sc.fsu.edu/~ameyerbaese) and Google Scholar.
labs.bridge: The one Scientific Computing faculty member whose department page explicitly lists computational neuroscience, so a CS/math student can do fMRI classification or cortical-network stability work without leaving a computing department.
labs.entry_point: fMRI data analysis and brain-based classification techniques (as listed on the department research page).

labs.name: PULSE Lab
labs.dept: Department of Scientific Computing
labs.focus: PULSE (Scientific Machine Learning Lab, founded 2022) does scientific machine learning for oceanography and health, including identification and classification of diseases from medical imaging (prostate and breast cancer detection on MRI) and physics-informed neural networks.
labs.how_to_apply: Lab site has a 'Join the lab' link (/join/) but no posted text was visible; no undergrad process stated.
labs.bridge: Hands-on deep learning on MRI and other scientific data in a computing department; the imaging-ML skill set transfers directly to neuroimaging labs, though no brain projects are listed (needs confirmation).
labs.entry_point: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sea Surface Data Assimilation in Operational Ocean Models (Ocean Science, 2025) as a representative scientific-ML project.

labs.name: Dexter Lab
labs.dept: Department of Scientific Computing
labs.focus: Deep learning, compressed sensing, uncertainty quantification, inverse problems, mathematical optimization, numerical analysis, computational epidemiology and computational genomics.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; department page links a personal site (sites.google.com/view/ndexter) and Google Scholar.
labs.bridge: Serves math/applied-math students who want rigorous foundations in deep learning, sparse recovery and inverse problems, the mathematics that underlies modern neural data analysis and imaging reconstruction.

labs.name: FSU Vision Group
labs.dept: Department of Computer Science
labs.focus: The FSU Vision Group works on computer vision and pattern recognition, including image understanding, object detection and segmentation, real-time vision systems, and computational models and algorithms for visual perception problems.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; page links only to https://www.cs.fsu.edu/~liux.
labs.bridge: The department page describes modeling visual perception computationally, so a CS student gets vision/ML training that maps onto visual-neuroscience questions.

labs.name: Chakraborty Lab
labs.dept: Department of Computer Science
labs.focus: Machine learning, computer vision and AI for healthcare, with an interest in intelligent learning algorithms under weak human supervision.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; personal site http://shayokch.com/ lists no students or openings.
labs.bridge: ML-for-healthcare and weak-supervision methods for CS majors; relevant to clinical neuro data pipelines but no brain data is listed (needs confirmation).

labs.name: Barbu Lab
labs.dept: Department of Statistics (affiliated faculty, Scientific Computing)
labs.focus: Computer vision, machine learning and medical imaging within biostatistics, with current projects in large-scale learning, robotic grasping and theoretical computer vision.
labs.how_to_apply: Department page states 'Recruiting a Graduate Student'; no undergrad process posted, personal site https://socrates.stat.fsu.edu/~abarbu/.
labs.bridge: A statistics-department route into ML and medical imaging for math/stats majors; department page says he is recruiting a graduate student and won the 2023 Graduate Faculty Mentor Award, undergrad route not stated.

labs.name: Optimal Robotics Lab
labs.dept: Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: The Optimal Robotics Lab studies robotics, bipedal locomotion, optimal control and biomechanical modeling, aiming to control legged robots to be as fast, maneuverable and stable as animals.
labs.how_to_apply: Lab site https://www.optimalroboticslab.com/ has a 'Join' menu item but no posted text; faculty page lists office hours Mon-Wed 3-5 pm, Room 217.
labs.bridge: Legged-locomotion control and biomechanical modeling give engineering students the motor-control and optimization vocabulary used in sensorimotor neuroscience; a college news page says he leads a team of undergraduate assistants (needs confirmation).

labs.name: STRIDe Lab
labs.dept: Department of Mechanical Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: The STRIDe Laboratory builds biologically inspired legged robots (Sprawl, RHex and Dynoclimber families) that run and climb, studying the dynamics, design and control of agile legged locomotion.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process and the old STRIDe lab site is gone; the 2024 FAMU-FSU College of Engineering page lists clarkj@eng.famu.fsu.edu, so email to ask whether the lab is taking students.
labs.bridge: Bio-inspired locomotion for mechanical/electrical engineers; the lab people page lists Undergraduate Research Assistants, though the visible roster is dated 2008-2009 and a 2024 college page still lists him as Professor of Mechanical Engineering (needs confirmation).

labs.name: Grant Lab
labs.dept: Department of Chemical & Biomedical Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: Magnetic resonance microscopy and high-field MRI (including the 21.1 T system at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory) applied to neurodegenerative diseases, muscular degeneration, bioengineered constructs, contrast mechanisms and single-cell diffusion and spectroscopy.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; research site https://sites.google.com/site/mrmicroscopyscgrantlab/ and BMES student chapter are the visible contact routes.
labs.bridge: The main FSU-side biomedical-engineering route into brain MRI at the MagLab; faculty page lists him as Professor and faculty supervisor of the BMES student chapter, though one college listing shows 'Professor Emeritus' so active status needs confirmation.
labs.entry_point: Magnetic resonance imaging with 21.1T and pathological correlations in diffuse Lewy body disease (listed on faculty page, no DOI given).

labs.name: DeBrunner Lab
labs.dept: Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
labs.focus: Signal processing, image processing and pattern recognition, including Hirschman optimal transforms, spectral estimation with compressive sensing, and hardware-efficient convolution.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process.
labs.bridge: Core DSP and pattern-recognition training for ECE students, the toolkit later used on EEG/LFP/spike data; no biomedical data is listed on the page.

labs.name: J. Fadool Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biological Science
labs.focus: Genetic and cellular mechanisms regulating photoreceptor development, patterning, retinal degeneration, and regeneration in zebrafish.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; the FSU OPDA profile describes trainees learning zebrafish genetics, imaging, and genomics before developing independent projects (needs confirmation that this extends to undergraduates).
labs.bridge: A classic biology entry point into sensory neuroscience: retina development and degeneration in a genetically tractable vertebrate, with imaging and genomics data a quantitatively minded student can grow into.
labs.entry_point: Sotolongo-Lopez et al. 2016, PLoS Genetics, on zebrafish photoreceptor specification (listed on the department page without DOI).

labs.name: Lyons Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biological Science
labs.focus: Molecular and cellular mechanisms by which sleep and the circadian clock affect neural plasticity, from drug tolerance to long-term memory.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; contact lyons@bio.fsu.edu (department page lists graduate recruiting for Fall 2021, so recruiting status needs confirmation).
labs.bridge: Memory and circadian rhythms are core comp-neuro topics; this lab gives a biology student the wet-lab plasticity and time-series behavioral background that models of sleep and memory are built on.
labs.entry_point: Lyons et al. 2020, Molecular Brain, on circadian/sleep effects on memory consolidation.

labs.name: Feng Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biological Science
labs.focus: Epigenetic regulation of neuropsychiatric disorders, with current projects on 3D chromosome architecture and TET1 DNA demethylation in addiction-engaged neuron subtypes of the ventral striatum.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; the page says the lab is recruiting graduate students and postdocs and lists feng@bio.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Genomics-heavy neuroscience: a biology student here will handle sequencing datasets, a natural on-ramp to bioinformatics and quantitative analysis of neural gene regulation.
labs.entry_point: Kaplan et al. 2022, Frontiers in Genetics, review of DNA epigenetics in addiction susceptibility.

labs.name: Brown Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biological Science (Program in Neuroscience)
labs.focus: Genetic and neural mechanisms regulating sleep and feeding, including how they change with aging and in a Drosophila model of Alzheimer's disease, and how the taste system distinguishes macronutrients.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile lists the lab as accepting graduate students and names two current graduate students.
labs.bridge: Fly neurogenetics with high-throughput behavioral readouts (sleep, feeding) is a common first lab for biology students who later move into quantitative behavior analysis and circuit modeling.

labs.name: Arbeitman Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: How complex behaviors are specified at the molecular-genetic level, focusing on mechanisms that create sex differences in the nervous system and underlie male and female reproductive behaviors.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile says the lab is accepting graduate students.
labs.bridge: Explicitly lists computational methods alongside wet-lab genomics, so a biology student can gain both fly neurogenetics and data-analysis experience in one lab.

labs.name: Kabbaj Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Neurobiology of individual and sex differences in depression and drug addiction, and epigenetic mechanisms of social bonding in prairie voles.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab page lists lab phone (850) 644-4930 and names graduate students, a research faculty member, and a lab assistant but no undergraduates.
labs.bridge: Behavioral neuroscience with a full molecular toolkit; best for biology or pre-health students who want stress/addiction neurobiology before any modeling.
labs.entry_point: Duclot, Lindsay, Koutakis, Wang & Kabbaj 2022, Biological Psychiatry (listed on lab page without DOI).

labs.name: Bhide Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine (Center for Brain Repair)
labs.focus: Developmental neurobiology centered on dopamine's role in brain development, linked to ADHD, early-onset torsion dystonia, and neurocognitive effects of pre- and early postnatal drug exposure.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile says accepting graduate students and links a College of Medicine directory page.
labs.bridge: Neurodevelopment and dopamine are foundational for later work on reinforcement-learning models; serves biology and pre-health students directly.

labs.name: Kumar Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Synaptic physiology of neocortical function and plasticity, focusing on AMPA and NMDA glutamate receptors and the ictogenic cells and circuits of the parahippocampal region in temporal lobe epilepsy.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile states not accepting graduate students and links a College of Medicine directory page.
labs.bridge: Electrophysiology and receptor kinetics are the raw material of biophysical neuron models; a biology student who learns patch-clamp here is well placed for Hodgkin-Huxley-style modeling later.

labs.name: Y. Wang Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: How the binaural circuit of the auditory brainstem forms, functions, and breaks down, focusing on the fragile X protein FMRP in chickens, mice, gerbils, and postmortem human brain tissue.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab site https://med.fsu.edu/wangyuanlab/home has a Lab Members page not read here (needs confirmation).
labs.bridge: The auditory brainstem binaural circuit is one of the best-modeled circuits in neuroscience (sound localization), so anatomical and developmental data from this lab connect directly to classic comp-neuro models.

labs.name: Zhou Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine
labs.focus: Developing and characterizing transgenic mouse models of schizophrenia and studying its neurobiology at the molecular, synaptic, and neural-circuit levels, including regulation of neuronal ion channels.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile states not accepting graduate students and lists zhou@neuro.fsu.edu.
labs.bridge: Ion-channel regulation and synaptic deficits in a disease model give a biology or pre-health student the cellular electrophysiology grounding that circuit models of psychiatric disease assume.

labs.name: Megraw Lab
labs.dept: Department of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine (Center for Brain Repair)
labs.focus: Centrosome and cilia function in cell division, development, and disease, including the MCPH primary-microcephaly proteins framed as a neural stem cell disease.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; profile links lab site https://med.fsu.edu/megrawLab/home and lists the course BMS4932 Current Research in Biomedical Sciences.
labs.bridge: A cell-biology lab for biology students interested in neurodevelopment (microcephaly, neural stem cells) rather than circuits; teaches Drosophila and imaging skills transferable to any neuro lab.
labs.entry_point: Zheng et al. 2020, Nature Cell Biology, on centrosome protein function.

labs.name: Li Lab
labs.dept: Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry / Institute of Molecular Biophysics
labs.focus: Atomic-level structure and mechanism of large molecular assemblies in gene expression, emphasizing RNA:protein, RNA:RNA, and protein:protein interactions.
labs.how_to_apply: No posted undergrad process; lab site has a people directory and contact page only.
labs.bridge: Not a neuroscience lab; it is the confirmed structural-biology entry point for a strictly-chemistry undergraduate who wants biomolecular structure skills before moving toward channel/receptor or neurodegeneration work.

types.label: Computational neuroscientist
types.blurb: Math-first: builds models of how neurons and circuits compute, and wants the model to be the work.

types.label: Computational biologist
types.blurb: Brings code and statistics to living systems: genes, cells and circuits, from sequencing data to animal models.

types.label: Neuroengineer
types.blurb: Wants to build things that read or write brain activity: signals, devices, closed loops.
jobs: Neurotech and medical device R&D engineer

types.label: Computational explorer
types.blurb: Comfortable writing code; curious how brains, and the AI modeled on them, compute.

types.label: Cognitive scientist
types.blurb: Studies how people think, decide, remember and perceive, with experiments on human participants.

types.label: Clinical researcher
types.blurb: Motivated by disorders and patients; wants research that could change how people are diagnosed or treated.

types.label: Experimental neuroscientist
types.blurb: Happiest at the bench: hands-on work with animals, tissue and circuits to see how brains really work.
